note: Steps of the plan, by milestone. gather.py keeps a 'done' or 'done-emu' step only while every pull request it names is merged with CI passing on the commit that brought it into main; otherwise it drops the step to 'review' or 'progress' and says why. The tag of each step (merged, in review, in progress or planned) comes from gh. 'done-emu' means checked on the host, in WASM under Node and Bun, or in headless DOSBox; nothing has run on real hardware. Milestones 0 to 5 are the working plan, with Milestone 1.5 (id m1_5) between Milestones 1 and 2; the order of Milestones 2 to 5 follows the restart plan in docs/POC-1-FINDINGS.md.

milestones.label: M1 · The first playable slice
milestones.next: The open pull requests (#39, #42, #45, #46 and #47), a pull request for the chicken's beak and captions, and the documentation phase.

milestones.label: M1.5 · Machine, settings and DOS audio
milestones.next: The DOS probes and /PROBE come first; fizz-machine (#44) is merged. The milestone is done when the cluck is audible on DOS, detection and settings work, and the frame-rate policy is measured.

milestones.label: M2 · Content pipeline
milestones.next: The real work has not started. The sprite grids and the generated sprite data exist; the first fizz-bake step is a Level Studio script baked into a Fizz Asset Pack (`.FAP`), with a per-target profile.

milestones.label: M3 · Scene intent and camera
milestones.next: The real work has not started. A shared pixel rule, a stateless look offset and the shared drawing exist; fizz-engine with scene intent is next, then the camera with Fizz 1's pixel-locking, shown on Web and DOS.

milestones.label: M4 · Audio
milestones.next: Builds on M1.5's detection and routing. The effects pipeline exists (the cluck source, the OPL2 and speaker downmixes, fizz-sfx and Web playback); the music work is to lower the IMF lab's composition to OPL2 and OPL3 arrangements for DOS and play it on Web.

milestones.label: M5 · CI gates and the 486 budget
milestones.next: Keeps the CI cycle gate and the size budgets. /BENCH, its calibration line and the tracked size exist; the budgets are measured against a 486DX model and gated in CI.

nodes.label: Input frames and hello-tick rules
nodes.what: Buttons, InputFrame and InputLatch in fizz-sim; the fizz-hello marker rules; the 600-tick M0_SCRIPT and the golden transcript.

nodes.label: fizz-hal
nodes.what: Clock and Pacer, Set 1 decoder, Display, SpscRing, and mock doubles.
nodes.evidence: cargo test -p fizz-hal; WebClock and DosClock are the two consumers of Clock

nodes.label: DOS runtime and packaging
nodes.what: fizz-dos-rt: start-up, DPMI, heap, IRQ 0 at 60 Hz, IRQ 1, mode 13h, clean-up; elf2go32.py; RTSMOKE.EXE.

nodes.label: Mode 13h presenter
nodes.what: fizz-present-dos: the 320x200 frame, palette, 8x8 font, HUD and key mapping, with golden frame checksums.

nodes.label: FIZZ2.EXE
nodes.what: The hello-tick program with /REPLAY, /LIVE and /PANIC, and tools/check-dos.sh.
nodes.evidence: FPU CW 027F, BIOS TICKS 182, VECTORS RESTORED yes, MOVED yes, PANIC exit 3

nodes.label: Web presenter
nodes.what: fizz-present-web, the static page and tools/build-web.sh; the replay run from the built module.
nodes.evidence: node tools/web-replay.mjs matches the golden transcript

nodes.label: Parity gate and CI job
nodes.what: tools/check-parity.sh and the parity job in the pinned ci-dos image.

nodes.label: Platform reference
nodes.what: docs/PLATFORM.md and the architecture update.

nodes.label: fizz-phys
nodes.what: An owned copy of Fizz 1's physics (pogo, tilemap, bodies) with the same constants, under the determinism discipline.
nodes.evidence: cargo test -p fizz-phys; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, Crate plan

nodes.label: Golden-trace tool
nodes.what: Golden traces recorded from Fizz 1's own simulation, and the tool that replays them against the Fizz 2 rules.

nodes.label: Key layouts
nodes.what: Jump, pogo and fire buttons, and Fizz 1's key layouts, shared by both presenters.

nodes.label: Sprite pipeline
nodes.what: The sprite grid pipeline and the export of Fizz 1's sprites to generated data.

nodes.label: Ben's port
nodes.what: Ben's movement ported from Fizz 1 and proved against the golden traces.

nodes.label: Slice world and replay
nodes.what: The slice level, the chicken, the red key and the door as rules, and a replay whose hash matches on native, Web and DOS.

nodes.label: View helpers
nodes.what: The camera and the software drawing helpers of fizz-view, shared by both presenters.
nodes.evidence: cargo test -p fizz-view; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, Web view

nodes.label: Slice drawing on both presenters
nodes.what: The slice drawn by the same routine on DOS (mode 13h, retrace wait) and the Web canvas, with Fizz 1's run cycle and the two-legged chicken.

nodes.label: Retire fizz-hello
nodes.what: The throwaway rules are deleted and the parity gate compares the slice instead.

nodes.label: The cluck as an event
nodes.what: The chicken's random cluck as a deterministic named event in the rules.

nodes.label: Cluck source with four variants
nodes.what: The cluck sound source, its OPL2 and speaker downmixes, fizz-sfx, and a repeated fourth variant.

nodes.label: Web audio with Undertone
nodes.what: The cluck played on the Web with Undertone; audio cannot be checked headlessly.

nodes.label: /BENCH and the drawing speed-up
nodes.what: The DOS /BENCH mode that times the step, the drawing and the copy; a faster slice drawing measured with it; and the corrected cycle setting.

nodes.label: The chicken's beak and captions
nodes.what: The chicken opens its beak and a caption floats when it clucks, with /NOCAPTIONS and /CAPTIONS on DOS. It is on a branch with no pull request yet.

nodes.label: Look and aim
nodes.what: Look up, look down and aim up and down, proven against Fizz 1.

nodes.label: Documentation phase
nodes.what: The player's manual, the reference documents and a refresh of this archive for the slice.

nodes.label: Machine model
nodes.what: fizz-machine: the pure start-up check and settings model, with the probe data, the resolver, the OPL write router and the screen builder, tested on the host.

nodes.label: DOS probes and /PROBE (P-B)
nodes.what: The DOS probes for the video adapter, the x87, the FM chip and the Sound Blaster, with a /PROBE mode that prints them.

nodes.label: /CHECK screen and /CHECKCELLS (P-C)
nodes.what: The opt-in text screen that shows what was found and the plan that follows, and /CHECKCELLS to inspect its cells.

nodes.label: Sound settings and FIZZ2.CFG v2 (P-D)
nodes.what: Sound settings stored in FIZZ2.CFG version 2, and the command-line flags that override them.

nodes.label: The /? help screen (P-E)
nodes.what: A help screen that lists the modes and flags.

nodes.label: DOS audio (P13)
nodes.what: The 560 Hz timer, the interrupt audio service, OPL2 channel 5, the PC speaker and the silent paths, so the cluck is audible on DOS.

nodes.label: OPL3 and the panned channel 14 (P-F)
nodes.what: OPL3 detection and effects on the panned channel 14.

nodes.label: Frame-rate policy and bench reporting
nodes.what: A frame-rate policy (auto, 60 Hz or 30 Hz), and /BENCH reporting per drawn frame.

nodes.label: Live HUD without TICK n
nodes.what: A live HUD that no longer prints the tick count.

nodes.label: Options screen
nodes.what: An Options screen that changes the settings; the last piece of the milestone.

nodes.label: fizz-bake
nodes.what: The host tool that bakes authored assets for each target into Fizz Asset Packs (`.FAP`). DOS parses nothing at start-up.

nodes.label: Level Studio scripts
nodes.what: Level and overworld scripts from Fizz Level Studio as the authoring format, possibly extended for vertical mazes and gadgets.

nodes.label: fizz-engine scene intent
nodes.what: Game, scene intent (tiles, sprites, lights, camera) and named events.

nodes.label: Camera with pixel-locking
nodes.what: Follow, look-ahead and look up and down as one deterministic module, with Fizz 1's pixel-locking.
nodes.evidence: Fizz 1 docs/ENGINE_SPEC.md: the camera snaps to the canvas-pixel grid each frame

nodes.label: Audio from the IMF lab source
nodes.what: A composition source played directly on Web and lowered to IMF or OPL2 for DOS, channel 5 kept for effects.

nodes.label: 486 cycle budget
nodes.what: A cycle estimate against a 486DX, since DOSBox at cycles=max hides x87 cost. Fizz 1's m5/bench and its estimator are the reference.

nodes.label: A real 486
nodes.what: FIZZ2.EXE on a physical 486DX with a VGA card and a real display.
